title: SciMON: Scientific Inspiration Machines Optimized for Novelty
abstract: Explicitly grounding language model outputs in retrieved inspirations from past scientific literature and iteratively optimizing for novelty will enable the generation of more novel, relevant, and technically detailed scientific ideas compared to standard language model approaches. Specifically, this paper investigates: Can neural language models generate novel scientific directions grounded in literature, moving beyond traditional binary link prediction to produce expressive, contextually rich hypotheses? How can the generation of scientific ideas be systematically optimized for novelty while maintaining relevance to existing literature?. A modeling framework, SCIMON, is proposed to generate novel scientific ideas by combining literature-grounded inspiration retrieval with iterative novelty optimization. The method begins by extracting background contexts (e.g., problems, motivations, experimental settings) and salient seed terms fro...
tldr: Can neural language models generate novel scientific directions grounded in literature, moving beyond traditional binary link prediction to produce expressive, contextually rich hypotheses? How can the generation of scientific ideas be systematically optimized for novelty while maintaining relevance to existing literature?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under automated scientific ideation & novelty search.
hypothesis: Explicitly grounding language model outputs in retrieved inspirations from past scientific literature and iteratively optimizing for novelty will enable the generation of more novel, relevant, and technically detailed scientific ideas compared to standard language model approaches.

title: LLM+P: Empowering Large Language Models with Optimal Planning Proficiency
abstract: Integrating large language models with classical symbolic planners via a structured translation pipeline will enable the generation of correct and optimal plans for complex tasks specified in natural language, outperforming LLMs used in isolation for planning. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can large language models be empowered to reliably solve complex, long-horizon planning problems specified in natural language, particularly in robotics and related domains?. A framework is developed that combines large language models (LLMs) with classical planning algorithms to solve planning problems described in natural language. The method first uses an LLM to translate a natural language problem description into a Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) problem ...
tldr: How can large language models be empowered to reliably solve complex, long-horizon planning problems specified in natural language, particularly in robotics and related domains?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under autonomous agent symbolic planning.
hypothesis: Integrating large language models with classical symbolic planners via a structured translation pipeline will enable the generation of correct and optimal plans for complex tasks specified in natural language, outperforming LLMs used in isolation for planning.

title: Masked Feature Prediction for Self-Supervised Visual Pre-Training
abstract: Predicting hand-crafted feature descriptors, such as Histograms of Oriented Gradients (HOG), for masked regions in visual data enables effective self-supervised pre-training of large-scale vision models, leading to improved performance on downstream video and image recognition tasks compared to previous methods that use pixel prediction, discrete tokenization, or deep network features. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can self-supervised learning methods be improved for visual pre-training, particularly for video understanding, without relying on external supervision or large-scale labeled datasets?. A self-supervised pre-training framework is developed in which a vision Transformer backbone processes visual input (video or image) with a portion of the input randomly masked out. The model is tasked with regressing feature representations of the masked regions, where the features are extracted fr...
tldr: How can self-supervised learning methods be improved for visual pre-training, particularly for video understanding, without relying on external supervision or large-scale labeled datasets?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under natural language understanding & reasoning.
hypothesis: Predicting hand-crafted feature descriptors, such as Histograms of Oriented Gradients (HOG), for masked regions in visual data enables effective self-supervised pre-training of large-scale vision models, leading to improved performance on downstream video and image recognition tasks compared to previous methods that use pixel prediction, discrete tokenization, or deep network features.

title: OUTFOX: LLM-generated Essay Detection through In-context Learning with Adversarially Generated Examples
abstract: Jointly training or prompting both the detector and the adversarial attacker to consider each other's outputs in an in-context learning framework will significantly improve the robustness and accuracy of LLM-generated essay detection, even under strong adversarial attacks, without sacrificing performance on non-attacked texts. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can the robustness of detectors for identifying LLM-generated essays be improved, particularly against adversarial attacks that adapt to the detector's outputs, and how can such detectors maintain high performance on both attacked and non-attacked texts?. A novel adversarial in-context learning framework, OUTFOX, is proposed to enhance the detection of LLM-generated essays. In this framework, both the detector and the attacker leverage each other's outputs as in-context examples within their respective prompts. The detector uses a mixture of human-wr...
tldr: How can the robustness of detectors for identifying LLM-generated essays be improved, particularly against adversarial attacks that adapt to the detector's outputs, and how can such detectors maintain high performance on both attacked and non-attacked texts?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under adversarial machine-generated text detection.
hypothesis: Jointly training or prompting both the detector and the adversarial attacker to consider each other's outputs in an in-context learning framework will significantly improve the robustness and accuracy of LLM-generated essay detection, even under strong adversarial attacks, without sacrificing performance on non-attacked texts.

title: SPARTA ALIGNMENT: Collectively Aligning Multiple Language Models through Combat
abstract: Collectively aligning multiple LLMs via a competitive, game-theoretic framework—where models generate, judge, and learn from each other's outputs—will yield superior alignment, greater generalization to unseen tasks, and enhanced output diversity compared to single-model self-alignment methods. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can the collective alignment of multiple large language models (LLMs) through competitive and collaborative mechanisms improve model alignment, generalization, and output diversity compared to single-model self-alignment approaches?. A novel algorithm, SPARTA ALIGNMENT, will be developed to collectively align a pool of LLMs through iterative competitive and collaborative processes. In each iteration, a prompt is sampled and two models are selected for a head-to-head 'combat', generating responses to the prompt. The remaining mod...
tldr: How can the collective alignment of multiple large language models (LLMs) through competitive and collaborative mechanisms improve model alignment, generalization, and output diversity compared to single-model self-alignment approaches?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under preference alignment & reinforcement learning.
hypothesis: Collectively aligning multiple LLMs via a competitive, game-theoretic framework—where models generate, judge, and learn from each other's outputs—will yield superior alignment, greater generalization to unseen tasks, and enhanced output diversity compared to single-model self-alignment methods.

title: On the Reliability of Watermarks for Large Language Models
abstract: Watermarks embedded in machine-generated text remain reliably detectable under a wide range of realistic modifications, including paraphrasing by humans or other language models and mixing with human-written content, provided that a sufficient quantity of text is available for analysis. Specifically, this paper investigates: How reliable are watermarking techniques for detecting machine-generated text from large language models in realistic, adversarial, and mixed-content scenarios, including paraphrasing by humans or other models and insertion into larger human-written documents?. A comprehensive evaluation will be conducted on the robustness of combinatorial watermarking schemes for large language models, focusing on both the watermark generation and detection pipelines. The watermarking method will involve seeding a pseudo-random function with a context window of preceding ...
tldr: How reliable are watermarking techniques for detecting machine-generated text from large language models in realistic, adversarial, and mixed-content scenarios, including paraphrasing by humans or other models and insertion into larger human-written documents?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under llm provenance & watermark verification.
hypothesis: Watermarks embedded in machine-generated text remain reliably detectable under a wide range of realistic modifications, including paraphrasing by humans or other language models and mixing with human-written content, provided that a sufficient quantity of text is available for analysis.

title: LLM in a flash: Efficient Large Language Model Inference with Limited Memory
abstract: It is hypothesized that by storing LLM parameters in flash memory and employing hardware-informed strategies to minimize data transfer and maximize throughput, it is possible to enable efficient inference of models larger than available DRAM, with significant reductions in latency and memory usage compared to naive loading approaches. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can large language models (LLMs) be efficiently run for inference on devices with limited DRAM capacity, particularly when the model size exceeds available memory, by leveraging flash memory and hardware-aware algorithmic optimizations?. The proposed method introduces a hardware-aware framework for LLM inference where model parameters are stored in flash memory and selectively loaded into DRAM on demand. An inference cost model is constructed to account for flash memory characteristics, guiding optimizations in two main areas: (1) r...
tldr: How can large language models (LLMs) be efficiently run for inference on devices with limited DRAM capacity, particularly when the model size exceeds available memory, by leveraging flash memory and hardware-aware algorithmic optimizations?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under resource-constrained model inference.
hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by storing LLM parameters in flash memory and employing hardware-informed strategies to minimize data transfer and maximize throughput, it is possible to enable efficient inference of models larger than available DRAM, with significant reductions in latency and memory usage compared to naive loading approaches.

title: Pride and Prejudice: LLM Amplifies Self-Bias in Self-Refinement
abstract: LLMs exhibit a measurable self-bias during self-refinement and self-rewarding processes, which can be amplified through iterative feedback and larger candidate pools, but this bias can be significantly reduced by increasing model size and incorporating external, accurate feedback. Specifically, this paper investigates: How does self-bias manifest and amplify in large language models (LLMs) during iterative self-refinement and self-rewarding pipelines across multiple tasks and languages, and what strategies can effectively mitigate this bias to improve downstream performance?. A formal definition of self-bias in LLMs will be established using two statistical measures: bias (the mean difference between LLM self-evaluation and human or reference-based evaluation) and distance skewness (the asymmetry of the distribution of these differences). The methodology involves prompti...
tldr: How does self-bias manifest and amplify in large language models (LLMs) during iterative self-refinement and self-rewarding pipelines across multiple tasks and languages, and what strategies can effectively mitigate this bias to improve downstream performance?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under self-refinement & recursive hallucination mitigation.
hypothesis: LLMs exhibit a measurable self-bias during self-refinement and self-rewarding processes, which can be amplified through iterative feedback and larger candidate pools, but this bias can be significantly reduced by increasing model size and incorporating external, accurate feedback.

title: Spike-driven Transformer
abstract: A Transformer architecture that is entirely spike-driven, using only sparse addition and binary spike communication, can achieve state-of-the-art accuracy on large-scale tasks while drastically reducing energy consumption compared to both conventional Transformers and existing spiking Transformer hybrids. Specifically, this paper investigates: Can the spike-driven paradigm of Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) be fully integrated into the Transformer architecture to achieve high task accuracy and extreme energy efficiency, making the model suitable for deployment on neuromorphic hardware?. A novel Transformer architecture is proposed in which all core computations, including self-attention and multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs), are re-designed to operate in a spike-driven manner. The key innovation is the Spike-Driven Self-Attention (SDSA) module, which replaces energy-intensive matrix m...
tldr: Can the spike-driven paradigm of Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) be fully integrated into the Transformer architecture to achieve high task accuracy and extreme energy efficiency, making the model suitable for deployment on neuromorphic hardware?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under neuromorphic energy-efficient attention.
hypothesis: A Transformer architecture that is entirely spike-driven, using only sparse addition and binary spike communication, can achieve state-of-the-art accuracy on large-scale tasks while drastically reducing energy consumption compared to both conventional Transformers and existing spiking Transformer hybrids.

title: LLM-Pruner: On the Structural Pruning of Large Language Models
abstract: It is hypothesized that a dependency-based structural pruning framework, combined with efficient importance estimation and rapid post-training using limited external data, can significantly compress large language models without substantial loss in their multi-task and generative performance. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can large language models be structurally pruned in a task-agnostic manner to reduce computational and memory requirements, while minimizing reliance on the original training data and preserving general-purpose language understanding and generation capabilities?. A novel framework, LLM-Pruner, is proposed for task-agnostic structured pruning of large language models. The method consists of three main stages: (1) Discovery of all coupled and interdependent structures within the model by constructing a dependency graph, ensuring that pruning respects the inher...
tldr: How can large language models be structurally pruned in a task-agnostic manner to reduce computational and memory requirements, while minimizing reliance on the original training data and preserving general-purpose language understanding and generation capabilities?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under resource-constrained model inference.
hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a dependency-based structural pruning framework, combined with efficient importance estimation and rapid post-training using limited external data, can significantly compress large language models without substantial loss in their multi-task and generative performance.

title: Magnetic Preference Optimization: Achieving Last-iterate Convergence for Language Models Alignment
abstract: A novel optimization framework that achieves last-iterate convergence to the Nash equilibrium of the original preference-based game will enable more accurate and efficient alignment of large language models with diverse human preferences, overcoming the limitations of existing average-iterate or regularized approaches. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can large language models be aligned with complex, potentially non-transitive human preferences in reinforcement learning from human feedback, while ensuring efficient and robust convergence to optimal policies?. A new algorithm, Magnetic Preference Optimization (MPO), will be developed to achieve last-iterate convergence to the Nash equilibrium (NE) of a two-player constant-sum game modeling human preferences. The method adapts Magnetic Mirror Descent (MMD) to the RLHF setting, introducing a periodically up...
tldr: How can large language models be aligned with complex, potentially non-transitive human preferences in reinforcement learning from human feedback, while ensuring efficient and robust convergence to optimal policies?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under preference alignment & reinforcement learning.
hypothesis: A novel optimization framework that achieves last-iterate convergence to the Nash equilibrium of the original preference-based game will enable more accurate and efficient alignment of large language models with diverse human preferences, overcoming the limitations of existing average-iterate or regularized approaches.

title: NodeFormer: A Scalable Graph Structure Learning Transformer for Node Classification
abstract: Learning layer-wise, adaptive latent graph structures via an efficient, differentiable operator will enable scalable, accurate node classification on large graphs, outperforming existing graph neural network and structure learning methods, particularly in challenging settings such as heterophily, long-range dependencies, and absent or incomplete input graphs. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can node classification on large-scale graphs be improved by learning adaptive, latent graph structures in a scalable and efficient manner, especially in scenarios with heterophily, long-range dependencies, incomplete or missing input graphs?. A new framework is proposed that introduces a scalable, Transformer-style graph neural network for node classification, named NODEFORMER. The core component is a kernelized Gumbel-Softmax operator that enables efficient, differentiable learning of discrete, layer-specific latent graph structures wit...
tldr: How can node classification on large-scale graphs be improved by learning adaptive, latent graph structures in a scalable and efficient manner, especially in scenarios with heterophily, long-range dependencies, incomplete or missing input graphs?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under natural language understanding & reasoning.
hypothesis: Learning layer-wise, adaptive latent graph structures via an efficient, differentiable operator will enable scalable, accurate node classification on large graphs, outperforming existing graph neural network and structure learning methods, particularly in challenging settings such as heterophily, long-range dependencies, and absent or incomplete input graphs.

title: Data Interpreter: An LLM Agent For Data Science
abstract: A hierarchical graph-based framework that decomposes data science workflows into dynamically managed subproblems, combined with programmable node generation for iterative code refinement and tool integration, will significantly improve the robustness, adaptability, and overall performance of LLM agents on complex data science tasks compared to existing methods. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can large language model (LLM) agents be designed to autonomously and robustly solve end-to-end data science workflows, including complex, interconnected tasks that require dynamic adaptation to evolving data and task dependencies?. The proposed approach introduces a hierarchical graph modeling framework for LLM-based data science agents. The workflow is decomposed into a task graph, where each node represents a major subproblem (e.g., data exploration, feature engineering, model training), and dependencies are represented as e...
tldr: How can large language model (LLM) agents be designed to autonomously and robustly solve end-to-end data science workflows, including complex, interconnected tasks that require dynamic adaptation to evolving data and task dependencies?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under natural language understanding & reasoning.
hypothesis: A hierarchical graph-based framework that decomposes data science workflows into dynamically managed subproblems, combined with programmable node generation for iterative code refinement and tool integration, will significantly improve the robustness, adaptability, and overall performance of LLM agents on complex data science tasks compared to existing methods.

title: GeoCLIP: Clip-Inspired Alignment between Locations and Images for Effective Worldwide Geo-localization
abstract: A CLIP-inspired image-to-GPS retrieval framework that directly aligns image features with continuous GPS location embeddings, using hierarchical positional encoding and contrastive learning, will achieve more accurate and data-efficient worldwide geo-localization than existing classification-based or image-to-image retrieval methods. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can the alignment between images and their corresponding geographic locations be improved to enable accurate and scalable worldwide geo-localization, especially in the absence of dense image galleries and with limited training data?. A novel image-to-GPS retrieval approach is proposed, where the task is formulated as matching a query image to a gallery of GPS coordinates rather than to a gallery of images. The method consists of two main components: an image encoder based on a frozen CLIP Vision Transformer (ViT-L/14) backbone w...
tldr: How can the alignment between images and their corresponding geographic locations be improved to enable accurate and scalable worldwide geo-localization, especially in the absence of dense image galleries and with limited training data?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under preference alignment & reinforcement learning.
hypothesis: A CLIP-inspired image-to-GPS retrieval framework that directly aligns image features with continuous GPS location embeddings, using hierarchical positional encoding and contrastive learning, will achieve more accurate and data-efficient worldwide geo-localization than existing classification-based or image-to-image retrieval methods.

title: Safe Latent Diffusion: Mitigating Inappropriate Degeneration in Diffusion Models
abstract: It is hypothesized that leveraging the internal representations and learned concepts of pre-trained diffusion models, without additional training or external classifiers, enables effective suppression of inappropriate content during image generation, thereby reducing undesired degeneration without degrading overall image fidelity or text alignment. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can the generation of inappropriate or biased content in text-to-image diffusion models be systematically measured and effectively mitigated, while preserving image quality and text alignment?. A novel safety guidance mechanism, termed Safe Latent Diffusion (SLD), will be developed for text-to-image diffusion models. SLD operates during inference by manipulating the latent space of the diffusion process, using classifier-free guidance to steer generations away from user-defined inappropria...
tldr: How can the generation of inappropriate or biased content in text-to-image diffusion models be systematically measured and effectively mitigated, while preserving image quality and text alignment?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under natural language understanding & reasoning.
hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging the internal representations and learned concepts of pre-trained diffusion models, without additional training or external classifiers, enables effective suppression of inappropriate content during image generation, thereby reducing undesired degeneration without degrading overall image fidelity or text alignment.

title: Reward Model Ensembles Help Mitigate Overoptimization
abstract: Ensemble-based conservative optimization objectives, such as worst-case optimization (WCO) and uncertainty-weighted optimization (UWO), will significantly reduce or eliminate overoptimization in RLHF pipelines, outperforming single reward model optimization, even in the presence of label noise. Specifically, this paper investigates: Can ensemble-based conservative optimization methods effectively mitigate the problem of overoptimization in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) for language model fine-tuning, especially under realistic conditions such as label noise?. The proposed approach involves training an ensemble of proxy reward models, each initialized with different random seeds but trained on the same dataset and with identical hyperparameters. During policy optimization, three ensemble-based objectives are considered: (1) mean optimization, which averag...
tldr: Can ensemble-based conservative optimization methods effectively mitigate the problem of overoptimization in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) for language model fine-tuning, especially under realistic conditions such as label noise?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under natural language understanding & reasoning.
hypothesis: Ensemble-based conservative optimization objectives, such as worst-case optimization (WCO) and uncertainty-weighted optimization (UWO), will significantly reduce or eliminate overoptimization in RLHF pipelines, outperforming single reward model optimization, even in the presence of label noise.

title: Register and CLS tokens yield a decoupling of local and global features in large ViTs
abstract: In large ViT models, the introduction of register tokens or the use of [CLS] tokens with residual connections leads to a decoupling of local patch features from global representations, thereby violating the patch integration assumption and reducing the interpretability of attention maps. Specifically, this paper investigates: How do register tokens and [CLS] tokens affect the relationship between local and global feature representations in large Vision Transformer (ViT) models, and what are the implications for model interpretability and the validity of the patch integration assumption?. A systematic analysis will be conducted on Vision Transformer models of varying sizes, both with and without register tokens, to quantify the degree to which global representations rely on local patch features versus register or [CLS] tokens. The methodology involves probing the attention distributi...
tldr: How do register tokens and [CLS] tokens affect the relationship between local and global feature representations in large Vision Transformer (ViT) models, and what are the implications for model interpretability and the validity of the patch integration assumption?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under natural language understanding & reasoning.
hypothesis: In large ViT models, the introduction of register tokens or the use of [CLS] tokens with residual connections leads to a decoupling of local patch features from global representations, thereby violating the patch integration assumption and reducing the interpretability of attention maps.

title: Unlocking the Potential of Model Calibration in Federated Learning
abstract: Dynamically adjusting the calibration penalty for each client in federated learning, based on the statistical similarity between local and global models, will improve both the calibration and accuracy of the global model across heterogeneous data distributions. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can model calibration be effectively integrated into federated learning to ensure reliable confidence estimates across heterogeneous client data distributions, without sacrificing model accuracy?. A novel framework, Non-Uniform Calibration for Federated Learning (NUCFL), is developed to integrate model calibration into federated learning (FL) by introducing a dynamic, client-specific calibration penalty during local training. The approach augments the standard FL loss with an auxiliary calibr...
tldr: How can model calibration be effectively integrated into federated learning to ensure reliable confidence estimates across heterogeneous client data distributions, without sacrificing model accuracy?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under natural language understanding & reasoning.
hypothesis: Dynamically adjusting the calibration penalty for each client in federated learning, based on the statistical similarity between local and global models, will improve both the calibration and accuracy of the global model across heterogeneous data distributions.

title: Learning to Clarify: Multi-turn Conversations with Action-Based Contrastive Self-Training
abstract: A quasi-online contrastive self-training approach that leverages action-based preference optimization can enable large language models to more efficiently learn dialogue policies for ambiguity recognition and clarification, outperforming standard supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization baselines in multi-turn conversational tasks. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can large language models be adapted to function as mixed-initiative conversational agents capable of effectively handling ambiguity and disambiguation in multi-turn conversations, particularly in data-scarce settings?. A novel framework, Action-Based Contrastive Self-Training (ACT), will be developed to adapt large language models for mixed-initiative conversational settings. The method models dialogue action planning as an implicit subtask of response generation, focusing on contrasting pragmatic conversational a...
tldr: How can large language models be adapted to function as mixed-initiative conversational agents capable of effectively handling ambiguity and disambiguation in multi-turn conversations, particularly in data-scarce settings?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under natural language understanding & reasoning.
hypothesis: A quasi-online contrastive self-training approach that leverages action-based preference optimization can enable large language models to more efficiently learn dialogue policies for ambiguity recognition and clarification, outperforming standard supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization baselines in multi-turn conversational tasks.

title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
abstract: A novel architecture that integrates linear attention mechanisms with recurrent structures, enabling both parallelized training and efficient, linear-time inference, will achieve performance comparable to state-of-the-art Transformers while significantly reducing computational and memory costs, especially for long sequences. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can a neural network architecture be designed to combine the efficient, linear-scaling inference of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with the parallelizable and expressive training capabilities of Transformers, in order to improve scalability and performance on large-scale sequence modeling tasks such as natural language processing?. A new model architecture, termed Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV), will be developed that reformulates the attention mechanism using a channel-wise, time-decay vector, allowing it to function as either a Transformer or an RNN. The architecture consists of stacked residual blocks, each containing...
tldr: How can a neural network architecture be designed to combine the efficient, linear-scaling inference of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with the parallelizable and expressive training capabilities of Transformers, in order to improve scalability and performance on large-scale sequence modeling tasks such as natural language processing?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under natural language understanding & reasoning.
hypothesis: A novel architecture that integrates linear attention mechanisms with recurrent structures, enabling both parallelized training and efficient, linear-time inference, will achieve performance comparable to state-of-the-art Transformers while significantly reducing computational and memory costs, especially for long sequences.

title: Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
abstract: It is hypothesized that reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), combined with preference modeling for helpfulness and harmlessness, can align large language models to be both helpful and harmless without degrading, and potentially improving, their performance on standard NLP and specialized skill evaluations. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can large language models be trained to act as helpful and harmless assistants using human feedback, and what are the effects of such alignment training on model performance, robustness, and the ability to integrate specialized skills?. The proposed method involves collecting separate datasets of human preferences for helpfulness and harmlessness through open-ended dialogue interactions with crowdworkers. Preference models (PMs) are trained on these datasets to evaluate model responses for helpfulness and harmlessness. These PMs ar...
tldr: How can large language models be trained to act as helpful and harmless assistants using human feedback, and what are the effects of such alignment training on model performance, robustness, and the ability to integrate specialized skills?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under natural language understanding & reasoning.
hypothesis: It is hypothesized that reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), combined with preference modeling for helpfulness and harmlessness, can align large language models to be both helpful and harmless without degrading, and potentially improving, their performance on standard NLP and specialized skill evaluations.

title: BOND: Aligning LLMs with Best-of-N Distillation
abstract: It is hypothesized that aligning the policy of a large language model to match the distribution of outputs produced by Best-of-N sampling, using a distribution matching approach based on Jeffreys divergence and iterative distillation, will enable the model to generate outputs of comparable quality to Best-of-N sampling with only a single sample at inference time, thus achieving superior reward/KL trade-offs and improved alignment with human preferences. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can large language models be aligned to emulate the high-quality outputs of Best-of-N sampling strategies, while avoiding the significant computational overhead at inference time associated with sampling and ranking multiple generations?. A novel RLHF algorithm, Best-of-N Distillation (BOND), will be developed to align the policy of a large language model with the distribution induced by Best-of-N sampling from a reference policy. The approach begins by analytically deriving the Best-of-N distribution, then formulates policy alignmen...
tldr: How can large language models be aligned to emulate the high-quality outputs of Best-of-N sampling strategies, while avoiding the significant computational overhead at inference time associated with sampling and ranking multiple generations?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under preference alignment & reinforcement learning.
hypothesis: It is hypothesized that aligning the policy of a large language model to match the distribution of outputs produced by Best-of-N sampling, using a distribution matching approach based on Jeffreys divergence and iterative distillation, will enable the model to generate outputs of comparable quality to Best-of-N sampling with only a single sample at inference time, thus achieving superior reward/KL trade-offs and improved alignment with human preferences.

title: Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers for Near-Infinite Context
abstract: It is hypothesized that by distributing blockwise self-attention and feedforward computations across multiple devices in a ring topology, and overlapping the communication of key-value blocks with computation, it is possible to scale Transformer context length linearly with device count, achieving near-infinite context size without additional overhead or loss of performance. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can the memory constraints of Transformers be overcome to enable efficient training and inference on extremely long sequences, scaling context length linearly with the number of devices, without incurring additional communication or computation overheads or resorting to attention approximations?. A novel framework, Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers, is proposed to address the memory bottleneck in large-context Transformer models. The method splits input sequences into blocks, assigning each block to a separate device in a ring topology. Each device computes blockwise self-attention ...
tldr: How can the memory constraints of Transformers be overcome to enable efficient training and inference on extremely long sequences, scaling context length linearly with the number of devices, without incurring additional communication or computation overheads or resorting to attention approximations?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under natural language understanding & reasoning.
hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by distributing blockwise self-attention and feedforward computations across multiple devices in a ring topology, and overlapping the communication of key-value blocks with computation, it is possible to scale Transformer context length linearly with device count, achieving near-infinite context size without additional overhead or loss of performance.

title: Preserve Your Own Correlation: A Noise Prior for Video Diffusion Models
abstract: Introducing a temporally correlated noise prior, rather than the conventional i.i.d. noise prior, during the fine-tuning of pretrained image diffusion models on video data will significantly improve the photorealism and temporal consistency of generated videos, while also enabling efficient knowledge transfer from image to video generation tasks. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can text-to-video diffusion models be efficiently trained to generate photorealistic and temporally coherent videos, especially in the context of limited large-scale video datasets and high computational costs?. A novel video diffusion noise prior will be developed to better align with the temporal correlations present in real video data. The approach involves fine-tuning a state-of-the-art pretrained text-to-image diffusion model (such as eDiff-I) jointly on large-scale image and video datasets. The conven...
tldr: How can text-to-video diffusion models be efficiently trained to generate photorealistic and temporally coherent videos, especially in the context of limited large-scale video datasets and high computational costs?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under natural language understanding & reasoning.
hypothesis: Introducing a temporally correlated noise prior, rather than the conventional i.i.d. noise prior, during the fine-tuning of pretrained image diffusion models on video data will significantly improve the photorealism and temporal consistency of generated videos, while also enabling efficient knowledge transfer from image to video generation tasks.

title: A theory of continuous generative flow networks
abstract: Generalized GFlowNets, equipped with appropriate theoretical foundations and training objectives, can efficiently and accurately sample from unnormalized target distributions over arbitrary state spaces, including those with continuous and hybrid structures, thereby retaining or surpassing the advantages observed in discrete GFlowNets. Specifically, this paper investigates: Can generative flow networks (GFlowNets) be extended to sample from unnormalized target distributions over general state spaces, including continuous and hybrid (discrete-continuous) domains, and what are the theoretical and practical implications of such a generalization for probabilistic inference and modeling tasks?. A comprehensive theoretical framework for generalized GFlowNets will be developed, extending existing flow-matching, detailed balance, and trajectory balance conditions to measurable pointed graphs that encompass both discrete and continuous state spaces. The methodology will formalize the necessary...
tldr: Can generative flow networks (GFlowNets) be extended to sample from unnormalized target distributions over general state spaces, including continuous and hybrid (discrete-continuous) domains, and what are the theoretical and practical implications of such a generalization for probabilistic inference and modeling tasks?
limitation: Degraded generalization and computational overhead under natural language understanding & reasoning.
hypothesis: Generalized GFlowNets, equipped with appropriate theoretical foundations and training objectives, can efficiently and accurately sample from unnormalized target distributions over arbitrary state spaces, including those with continuous and hybrid structures, thereby retaining or surpassing the advantages observed in discrete GFlowNets.

title: TIPS: Text-Image Pretraining with Spatial Awareness
abstract: Combining high-quality synthetic image captions with noisy web captions, together with integrating self-distillation and masked image modeling losses into a contrastive image-text pretraining framework, will result in image-text models that achieve spatially-aware and discriminative representations, leading to improved performance on both dense and global vision tasks. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can general-purpose image-text pretraining be enhanced to produce representations that are effective for both dense spatial understanding tasks and global vision tasks, enabling strong off-the-shelf performance in a wide variety of computer vision applications?. A new pretraining framework, Text-Image Pretraining with Spatial awareness (TIPS), will be developed to jointly optimize for spatially-aware and globally discriminative image representations. title: Diffusion for World Modeling: Visual Details Matter in Atari
abstract: Employing diffusion models as world models for reinforcement learning will enable more accurate modeling of environment dynamics, particularly in preserving critical visual details, leading to improved agent performance and sample efficiency relative to world models based on discrete latent variables. Specifically, this paper investigates: Can diffusion models, when adapted for world modeling, improve the fidelity of visual details and agent performance in reinforcement learning environments compared to existing discrete latent variable approaches?. title: Norm-guided latent space exploration for text-to-image generation
abstract: Guiding latent space exploration in text-to-image diffusion models using a norm-based prior derived from the statistical properties of the seed distribution will result in higher-quality image generation, improved semantic fidelity for rare concepts, and more efficient data augmentation for few-shot and long-tail learning tasks. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can the structure of the latent seed space in text-to-image diffusion models be better exploited to improve the quality and efficiency of image generation, particularly for rare concepts and few-shot learning scenarios?. title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series
abstract: A language modeling framework that tokenizes time series data via scaling and quantization, and trains standard transformer-based language models on these tokenized sequences, will enable effective probabilistic forecasting and strong zero-shot generalization, rivaling or surpassing both classical and deep learning baselines without requiring time-series-specific architectural modifications. Specifically, this paper investigates: Can a general-purpose, pretrained language model framework be developed for probabilistic time series forecasting, leveraging large-scale data and minimal architectural changes, to achieve strong in-domain and zero-shot forecasting performance across diverse datasets?. title: Proactive Privacy Amnesia for Large Language Models: Safeguarding PII with Negligible Impact on Model Utility
abstract: It is hypothesized that selectively forgetting only the key elements within memorized PII sequences, identified through sensitivity analysis, and compensating for any resulting performance loss via memory implanting, can effectively safeguard PII in large language models without significantly degrading their utility. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can large language models be protected from leaking personally identifiable information (PII) under adversarial attacks, while maintaining high model utility and performance?. title: VALOR: Vision-Audio-Language Omni-Perception Pretraining Model and Dataset
abstract: Jointly modeling relationships among vision, audio, and language in an end-to-end framework, using strongly correlated tri-modal data and novel pretraining tasks, will significantly improve generalization and performance on a wide range of multimodal downstream tasks compared to dual-modality or weakly correlated approaches. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can a unified pretraining framework be developed to enable comprehensive understanding and generation across vision, audio, and language modalities, and what are the benefits of leveraging large-scale, strongly correlated tri-modal datasets for such models?. A novel omni-perception pretraining model, VALOR, will be constructed to jointly encode and align vision, audio, and language modalities. title: Unlearn What You Want to Forget: Efficient Unlearning for LLMs
abstract: It is possible to efficiently unlearn specific data from LLMs by introducing lightweight, parameter-efficient unlearning layers trained with a selective teacher-student objective, and by fusing multiple such layers to handle sequential deletion requests, thereby preserving model performance on retained data and tasks. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can large language models (LLMs) efficiently and effectively remove the influence of specific user-requested data (such as privacy-related or erroneous data) without retraining the entire model, while maintaining predictive quality and supporting sequences of unlearning operations?. title: STAR: A Benchmark for Situated Reasoning in Real-World Videos
abstract: Current state-of-the-art visual reasoning and video question answering models are insufficient for robust situated reasoning in real-world videos, and a benchmark that combines structured situation abstraction with logic-grounded question answering will reveal key challenges and guide the development of more capable reasoning systems. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can machine intelligence be evaluated and advanced in its ability to perform situated reasoning in real-world video scenarios, specifically involving dynamic, compositional, and logical understanding of human-object interactions, temporal sequences, action prediction, and feasibility inference?. A comprehensive benchmark will be constructed to evaluate situated reasoning in real-world videos, focusing on four core reasoning skills: interaction understanding, temporal sequence reasoning, action prediction, and feasibility inference. title: DragDiffusion: Harnessing Diffusion Models for Interactive Point-Based Image Editing
abstract: Harnessing large-scale pretrained diffusion models and optimizing the latent at a single, carefully selected diffusion step, combined with identity-preserving fine-tuning and reference-latent-control, will enable accurate, efficient, and robust interactive point-based image editing that generalizes well to both real and synthetic images. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can interactive point-based image editing be made more accurate, controllable, and generalizable across diverse image domains using large-scale generative models?. A novel framework will be developed for interactive point-based image editing by leveraging pretrained diffusion models, specifically Stable Diffusion. title: Accelerating RL for LLM Reasoning with Optimal Advantage Regression
abstract: Directly approximating the optimal advantage function using offline sampling from a reference policy, followed by on-policy updates via least-squares regression with a single generation per prompt, will enable efficient and effective RL-based fine-tuning of LLMs for reasoning tasks, reducing computational overhead and memory usage while maintaining or improving performance. Specifically, this paper investigates: Can reinforcement learning algorithms for large language model (LLM) reasoning be made more computationally efficient and scalable, particularly for long-context and complex reasoning tasks, without sacrificing performance?. title: Generating Graphs via Spectral Diffusion
abstract: A generative model that operates in the spectral domain by learning to generate eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the graph Laplacian via a diffusion process, followed by a permutation-invariant graph predictor, will enable efficient, scalable, and accurate graph generation, including the ability to condition on spectral properties and handle node features. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can graph generative models be designed to efficiently and accurately generate graphs that capture complex structural characteristics, node features, and spectral properties, while scaling to large graphs and enabling conditioning on desired spectral attributes?. title: Toward Extreme Image Compression With Latent Feature Guidance and Diffusion Prior
abstract: Incorporating a two-stage framework that combines compressive variational autoencoders with pre-trained diffusion models, guided by latent feature alignment and conditional diffusion decoding, will enable realistic and high-fidelity image reconstruction at extremely low bitrates, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can extreme image compression at very low bitrates (below 0.1 bits per pixel) be achieved while maintaining high perceptual quality and fidelity in reconstructed images, particularly by leveraging advanced generative models?. title: Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning with Classifier-Free Diffusion Generation
abstract: Utilizing classifier-free guidance within a diffusion model to simultaneously augment both offline and online data will generate higher-quality, better-aligned samples, leading to improved performance and stability in offline-to-online reinforcement learning compared to existing data augmentation methods. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can data augmentation methods be improved to better align generated data with the online policy distribution in offline-to-online reinforcement learning, thereby enhancing the performance and stability of RL agents during online fine-tuning?. A novel data augmentation framework is proposed that employs classifier-free guidance in diffusion models to generate synthetic data for both offline and online distributions in offline-to-online reinforcement learning (O2O RL). title: Ring-A-Bell! How Reliable are Concept Removal Methods for Diffusion Models?
abstract: Existing safety mechanisms and concept removal methods in text-to-image diffusion models are insufficiently robust and can be circumvented by systematically crafted adversarial prompts, even without access to the underlying model parameters. Specifically, this paper investigates: How reliable are current concept removal and safety mechanisms in text-to-image diffusion models at preventing the generation of inappropriate or forbidden content, and can their limitations be systematically exposed through automated prompt-based evaluation?. A model-agnostic red-teaming framework, Ring-A-Bell, will be developed to evaluate the effectiveness of safety mechanisms in text-to-image diffusion models. title: Studying Large Language Model Generalization with Influence Functions
abstract: Influence functions, when efficiently scaled to large language models, can reveal meaningful and interpretable patterns of generalization, abstraction, and memorization by identifying which training sequences most affect specific model behaviors. Specifically, this paper investigates: How can the generalization behavior of large language models be systematically analyzed by attributing model outputs to specific training data, and what patterns of generalization, abstraction, and memorization emerge as model scale increases?. A scalable framework will be developed for computing influence functions in large transformer-based language models using the Eigenvalue-corrected Kronecker-Factored Approximate Curvature (EK-FAC) approximation to efficiently estimate inverse-Hessian-vector products (IHVPs). hypothesis: Influence functions, when efficiently scaled to large language models, can reveal meaningful and interpretable patterns of generalization, abstraction, and memorization by identifying which training sequences most affect specific model behaviors.
